name: Future House
about: Future house is the name Tchami gave in 2013 to a slick, bass-heavy strain of deep house: a shuffled four-to-the-floor, a metallic, formant-filtered bassline that talks in the gaps, pitched-down vocal chops and a clean, loud Dutch mix. Oliver Heldens' Gecko and Koala, released through Tiësto's Musical Freedom and Spinnin', made it the sound of 2014, and Don Diablo's Hexagon label, Mesto, Brooks and Mike Williams turned it into a festival staple. Its DNA comes from UK garage and Disclosure's Settle, but it is a producer's and DJ's genre, built around singles and radio shows rather than albums. Fans rightly insist it is better than its reputation; critics rightly note how few full-lengths exist.

artists.name: Oliver Heldens
artists.why: Gecko made it a chart sound

albums.title: Settle
albums.why: The Lawrence brothers' debut revived UK garage as pop house with Latch and White Noise, and every future house producer learned its bass and vocal tricks.

albums.title: Sirens
albums.why: London's Gorgon City followed Settle with a vocal-led deep house album, Ready for Your Love included, that sits at the pop end of the sound.

albums.title: Generationwhy
albums.why: Faded's anonymous producer made a moody, song-based deep house album with the bass weight future house borrowed; In the Morning is the keeper.

albums.title: Future
albums.why: The Hexagon boss's first full album is the genre's clearest long-form statement, polished future house with pop vocals and a few real hooks.

albums.title: The Wise and the Wicked
albums.why: A concept double album of bass house and future house from the Bite This founder; too long, but the heavier tracks show why he filled festival tents.

albums.title: Outsiders
albums.why: The Night Bass label head's debut album is the American bass house strain, garage-derived, raw and built for the club rather than the radio.

albums.title: Between Us
albums.why: The Future Classic producer's debut is sunlit Australian house with the vocal chops and warm bass future house shares; Numb is the standout.

albums.title: Year Zero
albums.why: Tchami's long-awaited debut treats future house as gospel-tinged pop, with Proud and Ghosts; the genre's inventor finally in album form.

albums.title: Duality
albums.why: The British producer behind Need U (100%) delivers a sleek, melodic house album, Ocean Drive and Red Light Green Light included.

albums.title: Energy
albums.why: Faster and more global than Settle, with Fatoumata Diawara and Aminé, Energy is Disclosure's most club-focused record.

albums.title: FORΞVΞR
albums.why: The second Hexagon album stretches future house toward pop and orchestral gestures; ambitious, uneven, and best in its club moments.

albums.title: Olympia
albums.why: A lockdown-era album of melodic house with guest vocalists; well produced and unadventurous, the sound's mature middle age.

note: Future house is a singles genre with few albums; this shelf includes the garage-house roots and bass house neighbours that shaped it.
